title: Smoky Chicken and Sweet Potato Skillet Hash
intro: A covered-skillet steaming trick makes this meal fast to prepare. Tender sweet potatoes, smoky chicken thighs, and hearty kale anchor a satisfying, high-fiber hash.

ingredients.name: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.canonical_name: Chicken, broilers or fryers, thigh, meat only, raw

ingredients.name: Low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.canonical_name: Soup, chicken broth, low sodium, canned

ingredients.name: Raw pumpkin seeds (pepitas)
ingredients.canonical_name: Seeds, pumpkin and squash seeds, whole, raw

instructions: Toss the chicken with the smoked paprika, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper in a medium bowl.
Heat the oil in a large skillet with a tight-fitting lid over medium-high heat. Add the seasoned chicken and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until browned on the outside, then transfer it to a plate.
Add the sweet potatoes and red onion to the same skillet. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring to pick up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Pour in the chicken broth and immediately cover the skillet. Reduce the heat to medium-low and steam for 6 to 8 minutes, checking at 6 minutes, until the sweet potatoes are tender.
Uncover the skillet and stir in the kale. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes until the leaves begin to wilt.

Return the chicken and any resting juices to the skillet. Drizzle with the apple cider vinegar and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the chicken is completely cooked through and the moisture has mostly evaporated.
Divide the hash between plates and top with the pumpkin seeds before serving.
variation: Swap the chopped kale for fresh spinach or Swiss chard.
conservation: Keeps 2 to 3 days refrigerated; reheat in a warm skillet.
validation_warnings: [chapter_intent_fit] Mostly on-brief for the main dinner chapter, but the automated check flags it as slightly overshooting the strict 550 mg sodium ceiling (hitting ~585 mg). Reduce the added salt from 1/4 tsp to 1/8 tsp to cleanly clear the gate; the dish will remain plenty savory thanks to the smoked paprika, broth, and vinegar.
